mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) signals strong housing market activity, which correlates with rising consumer confidence and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved economic outlook.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations contract under higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer credit (RSAFS) indicate a weakening housing market and reduced consumer spending, which together predict negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic activity contracts.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings face headwinds from reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS declines by at least 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to delayed monetary policy responses and increased equity risk premiums, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in higher future interest rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with CPIAUCSL increasing by at least 0.2% month-over-month, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% (UNRATE > 5.0%), it signals a weakening labor market that reduces household income and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as equity valuations adjust to lower growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates and reduced real income, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In industrial slowdown regimes (INDPRO < 95.0), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates reduced manufacturing output and weak business investment, which correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings face sector-wide headwinds.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.
